key_facts: No remarkable medical or family history
Previous treatment with topical steroid ointments and oral compound glycyrrhizin tablets had no effect
Palms, soles, and oral mucosa are not involved
Laboratory tests showed no abnormal findings
Skin biopsy revealed mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and atrophy of the epidermis
Histopathology showed well-developed cornoid lamellae and individual cell dyskeratosis
Slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including intensively pruritic papules and the histopathological findings of cornoid lamellae, parakeratosis, and individual cell dyskeratosis, are consistent with Grover's disease.

rejected.label: Eruptive pruritic papular porokeratosis
rejected.why: While it shares some similar symptoms, the histopathological findings do not fully align with this condition.

rejected.label: Darier's disease
rejected.why: The lack of characteristic suprabasal acantholytic dyskeratosis in the histopathology does not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
rejected.why: The absence of characteristic palmoplantar keratoderma and the specific histopathological features of PRP do not align with the patient's presentation.
